name: De Vinne Condensed 6pt 1900
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office and American Type Founders; the collective ATF page credits Central Type Foundry, St. Louis, for the design
description: 6-point De Vinne Condensed with flared serifs, a descending Q tail, double-storey a and g, and complete observed alphabets and figures.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures, plus the observed comma. Space has a modern layout advance. Other punctuation requires source evidence. No aliases or invented companions. The date identifies the retained complete census alphabet, supplemented by matching earlier ATF impressions.
observed: The census specimen shows both complete 6-point alphabets and all ten figures. Matching ATF impressions supply clearer letters and figures. Seven retained native pages document repeated samples and source-quality comparisons.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform scaling within each physical source, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. Named alternatives preserve observed R constructions. No independent width stretching or cross-size substitution.
